ai.title: System prompt adds export grep rule and scope limits
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts instructs agent to grep references before renaming exported symbols and restricts file access to current working directory. Response format tightened to strictly execute user requests without extrapolation. knowledge.md adds Project Goals section prioritizing developer productivity and power user focus. Internal prompt engineering change affecting agent behavior across all surfaces.

eli5.text: The assistant now double-checks its work before renaming things, grepping to find all other places that reference a function, class, or variable so they get updated too. It's also taught to stay within the current project folder and answer more directly without guessing what you might want. A new section was added documenting that the project's priorities are making developers more productive and helping power users move faster. These are internal changes to how the assistant behaves, so you wouldn't see a new button or feature, but you might notice it's more careful with code edits and doesn't wander into other directories.

ai.title: Fix gitignore leading slash handling in project-files.ts
ai.summary: parseGitignore in npm-app/src/project-files.ts strips leading slashes from gitignore lines before adding to ignore instance. loadAllProjectFiles removed as redundant. getProjectFileTree uses defaultIgnore instead of rootIgnore. Version bumped to 1.0.28 in npm-app/package.json.

eli5.text: The assistant now correctly reads your gitignore file, which tells it which project files to skip. Previously, the leading slash in gitignore rules could cause files that should be ignored to still be included in scans. Now those files are properly excluded, so the assistant gets a cleaner view of your project's relevant files without clutter from ignored paths.

ai.title: Move printFileTree to common file util
ai.summary: Relocates the printFileTree function from backend/src/system-prompt.ts to common/src/util/file.ts. This centralizes file tree formatting logic within the shared utility module, removing the local implementation from the backend system prompt generator. The change affects only internal code structure without altering runtime behavior or user-facing features.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions for showing you a list of your project files were moved from one internal file to another shared location. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping: you won't notice any difference in how file lists appear, and nothing about your experience changed. The move just consolidates the logic so the same formatting rule can be reused everywhere instead of living in only one part of the system. It's live today with no behavior change.

ai.title: Move prompt instructions to system prompt
ai.summary: Relocates `scrape_web_page` and knowledge file editing instructions from `main-prompt.ts` to `system-prompt.ts`. `main-prompt.ts` now only appends the `STOP_MARKER` to user messages. `system-prompt.ts` integrates these rules into the numbered workflow list, shifting existing steps down. This centralizes behavioral guidance in the system context.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions were reorganized: the rules guiding how it searches files and updates its learning notes were moved from one set of instructions to another, more central set that applies to all its behavior. Where it works: backend source files. Who it affects: the assistant's own reasoning, not anything you change in the app. What you'd notice: nothing directly, since this is behind-the-scenes housekeeping, but if you looked at the change you'd see the same guidance now listed as part of the assistant's overall workflow rather than tacked onto each user message.

ai.title: Pre-fetch relevant files via Haiku before main prompt
ai.summary: New `requestRelevantFiles` function uses Haiku to identify files from the project tree and message history. These files are pre-fetched and injected into the last user message under `<relevant_files>`, replacing the previous instruction for Claude to manually list and read directories. The system prompt is updated to remove the file-reading steps, assuming context is already provided. This change affects `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`, and `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: The coding assistant no longer needs to manually browse your project's folders to find relevant files before answering your request. Instead, a quick, lightweight scan now happens first to identify and pre-load the most relevant files based on your project structure and conversation history, then passes them directly to the main assistant. You'll notice the assistant starts working with the right files already open, saving the time it previously spent figuring out which directories and files to read.

ai.title: Update knowledge.md with backend prompts, WebSocket flow, and tool
ai.summary: Documentation expanded across `backend/knowledge.md`, `knowledge.md`, and `npm-app/knowledge.md`. Added sections detailing the Request Files Prompt (`src/request-files-prompt.ts`), WebSocket communication flow, file versioning (`CTRL+U`/`CTRL+R`), and CLI key handling. Tool handlers (`read_files`, `scrape_web_page`, `search_manifold_markets`, `run_terminal_command`) and security considerations documented.

eli5.text: The team expanded the internal guides that explain how the assistant works behind the scenes across three documentation files. These guides now spell out how the assistant picks up the right files, sends and receives messages in real time, and handles new mini-programs like reading files or running commands. If you opened one of these guide files, you would see new sections walking through these pieces and the safety rules that go with them. Nothing you can touch in the product changed; these notes are for people building the assistant.

ai.title: Fix import path in request-files-prompt
ai.summary: Corrected import path for `ProjectFileContext`, `printFileTree`, and `createFileBlock` in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`. Changed source from `common/src/util/file` to `common/util/file`. This resolves module resolution errors in the backend build. Scope limited to backend request handling.

eli5.text: The backend was trying to load a shared utility module using an incorrect path, like asking someone to fetch a book from the wrong shelf number. Internal developers will no longer see the backend fail to compile due to a module resolution error when referencing file-handling tools. No user-facing behavior changes; the system continues working as before once built.

ai.title: Parallel key and comprehensive file requests
ai.summary: requestRelevantFiles now executes parallel Claude calls using models.sonnet for a focused key-file prompt and models.haiku for a comprehensive prompt. Results merge via Set deduplication to balance precision and recall. Internal backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts only. Key prompt hard-caps selection at approximately 6 files.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to look at files to understand your project, it now sends out two searches at the same time: one that looks hard for the few most important files, and one that looks broadly for many possibly-useful files. It then combines both results, removing any duplicates. If you watched the assistant gather context, you would see it pull about 6 key files plus additional supporting files in a single combined batch instead of one slow pass. This change is internal and already live today.

ai.title: Prompt ordering instructions added
ai.summary: Added explicit ordering instructions to prompt templates in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`. Changes instruct the model to order relevant files by importance, first. Internal prompt engineering adjustment.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions now tell it to think hardest about which files matter most before listing them. When you ask for help, any files the assistant gathers to read on your behalf will show up in a ranking, with the most important ones at the top. A developer on the team will notice this when writing prompts, but for anyone who simply asks the assistant questions, nothing new appears in the chat.

ai.title: Update backend knowledge doc
ai.summary: backend/knowledge.md restructured to reflect current Manicode architecture. Project Structure section replaced by Architecture Overview. New sections added: Tool Handling, Error Handling and Debugging, Build and Deployment, Security Considerations. TODO list updated with diff generation optimization item.

eli5.text: The internal guide describing how your assistant's backend works has been reorganized. Instead of just listing files and folders, the document now explains how the system fits together (Node.js plus TypeScript, an Express web server, and a WebSocket connection for real-time chat), how tools like reading files or scraping web pages are called and returned, how errors and logging work, how the code is built and deployed, and what security rules apply. The old project-folder layout section was replaced, and a few new topics were added, including a note about speeding up how file changes are figured out. This is a behind-the-scenes documentation update, so it does not change anything you see or do today, it just makes the system's design clearer for maintainers.

ai.title: Refine relevant file logging and dedup
ai.summary: Removed verbose timing logs from `requestRelevantFiles`. Switched dedup to `uniq`. Added dynamic timing/response logs in `getRelevantFiles`. Prompt updated to mention `read_files` tool.

eli5.text: The assistant's behind-the-scenes file discovery got tidier: it now removes duplicate file mentions more simply and skips some noisy internal timing messages, while adding cleaner timing and response logs where they matter. You won't see any difference in the answers you get, but the system that picks which files to show the assistant now does that job more cleanly and logs only what's useful for debugging.

ai.title: Stream file reads, flatten tree schema
ai.summary: Backend streams file read notifications via onResponseChunk in backend/src/main-prompt.ts. ProjectFileContextSchema.fileTree changed from single FileTreeNode to array in common/src/util/file.ts. printFileTree and getProjectFileTree in npm-app/src/project-files.ts updated to handle root-level arrays, removing implicit project root node.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads files for you, you'll now see a message like 'Reading the following files...' followed by their names, so you know what it's looking at. The file structure shown no longer includes your project's top-level folder name, instead starting directly with the contents inside it. This applies to everyone using the tool today.
